title.narrative: Support to International Commission on Missing Persons
Support to International Commission on Missing Persons

description.narrative:
Outcome A: Capacities of relevant authorities involved in the process of accounting for missing persons in Kosovo further strengthened; Outcome B: Continued engagement of families of missing persons in the process of accounting for Kosovo conflict missing persons; Outcome C: Regional cooperation to address the issue of persons missing from the Kosovo conflict enhanced.
On Outcome A:
- Cases of unidentified human remains in Institute of Forensic Medicine mortuary forensically reviewed and recommendations for case resolution provided to the Kosovo authorities - Biological samples from exhumations in Kosovo and Serbia are DNA tested and matched for the purpose of human identification of missing persons - Designated staff from the Institute for Forensic Medicine trained in use of Total Station at exhumations and in post-mortem examination and sampling - Kosovo Agency on Forensics capacities in DNA analysis for the purpose of human identification of conflict-related missing persons cases strengthened
On Outcome B: - Families of missing persons better informed on the process of accounting for missing persons in Kosovo, and awareness of youth and the general public in Kosovo on the issue of missing persons raised
On Outcome C: - Increased cooperation between Kosovo and Serbia government commissions on missing persons to account for missing persons

Projektet syftar till att bygga och stärka kapaciteten hos berörda myndigheter som är involverade i processen att redovisa försvunna personer i Kosovo; att engagera familjer till saknade personer som håller på att redogöra för saknade personer i Kosovokonflikten; och att förbättra regionalt samarbete för att ta itu med frågan om personer som saknas från Kosovokonflikten.

The project aims to build and strenthen the capacities of relevant authorities involved in the process of accounting for missing persons in Kosovo; to engage families of missing persons in the process of accounting for Kosovo conflict missing persons; and to enhance regional cooperation to address the issue of persons missing from the Kosovo conflict.

description.narrative:
During the reporting period from 1 September 2024 to 31 August 2025, implementation of the Sida-supported project Accounting of Missing Persons as a Result of the Conflict in Kosovo, 19982000 has progressed in a steady and results-oriented manner. Within the overall framework of SEK 9,996,000 for 20222026, the most significant achievements relate to strengthened institutional capacity, enhanced forensic infrastructure, and continued identification of missing persons.
A key priority has been reinforcing the capacity of the Government Commission on Missing Persons (GCMP). The harmonization and transfer of historical exhumation data into the Integrated Data Management System represent a major structural improvement, ensuring that Kosovo institutions now manage comprehensive and standardized records. Targeted trainings and joint technical sessions further strengthened cooperation, data accuracy, and case management.
Equally important has been the strengthening of the Kosovo Agency on Forensics (KAF). The donation of essential laboratory equipment, alongside additional planned procurements, has significantly improved KAFs ability to process, analyze, and store DNA samples in line with international forensic standards. This investment enhances sustainability and national ownership of the identification process.
Operationally, DNA testing and matching continued to deliver concrete outcomes. The submission of 97 DNA reports (107 including re-associations) to the Kosovo authorities resulted in new identifications and case clarifications, contributing to a reduction in active missing persons cases from 1,598 in August 2023 to 1,556 in November 2025. Although incremental, this decrease reflects measurable progress.
Regional cooperation, facilitated through trilateral meetings, enabled the harmonization and closure of additional cases, while the Small Grants Programme strengthened engagement with family associations and civil society, promoting transparency and maintaining public trust in the process.
Overall performance during this period is assessed as satisfactory and in line with project objectives, despite ongoing political sensitivities. However, the number of unresolved cases remains high, underscoring the continued urgency of sustained institutional, technical, and regional efforts until the fate of every missing person is clarified.
